messages:
andrew: FYI customer (FinReg Inc) escalated: their SIEM shows gaps for 2025-01-14 -> some audit events missing after we rolled out the KMS-redaction change.
maria: Link to the case and sample files?
andrew: Case# 98721. S3 path they pulled: s3://redwood-audit-exports/prod/finreg/2025-01-14/part-0003.avro. They say expected ~120k events, file only has ~18k.
andrew: They also see schema mismatches in the SIEM mapping for `request.user_agent` -> sometimes present, sometimes null.
kevin: Can you dump the forwarder logs for that timeframe? ingester should emit batch size and encryption metadata.
ingest-bot: [automated] Found forwarder run: forwarder-run-id=fr-20250114-17; files produced: 8; total_events=94432; uploaded_files=8; upload_errors=1 -> error=KMS:DecryptError
sarah: The KMS error is suspicious. If a single file failed to decrypt on our consumer it could look like "missing events" if we dropped that batch. Which file had upload_errors=1?
ingest-bot: upload_error_file=s3://redwood-audit-exports/prod/finreg/2025-01-14/part-0007.avro; producer-log: UploadComplete but put-object returned 200 with x-amz-server-side-encryption:aws:kms, client shows success. Consumer log shows DecryptError when decrypting envelope.
kevin: That points to a key-policy/rotation mismatch. Did we recently rotate the KMS CMK or switch to an external HSM-wrapped key for Dedicated customers?
maria: I rolled a key alias swap on 2025-01-14 15:02 UTC for the audit-export CMK as part of compliance patch. Policy change was supposed to be read-only to exporters; might have blocked decrypt with old envelope format.
andrew: Customer insists we never changed retention/filters on their account. They saw entirely missing event types (auth.*) — not just a single contiguous window. Could be sampling or schema-level filtering earlier in pipeline.
sarah: Two hypotheses: 1) one forwarder batch failed decrypt and we retried only parts, resulting in partial gaps across types; 2) our schema flattening step dropped nested fields causing the SIEM mapping to treat events as unmatched and they appear missing.
kevin: Repro steps: copy the reported file locally, run the consumer decrypt with current KMS key:
```
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-audit-exports/prod/finreg/2025-01-14/part-0007.avro ./
./audit-consumer --decrypt --kms-key-alias alias/exporter-audit --input part-0007.avro
```
If DecryptError, check key ARN and key usage metadata in CloudTrail: Lookup Encrypt/Decrypt calls for fr-20250114-17.
maria: I pulled cloudtrail: there was a ReEncrypt/GenerateDataKey call at 2025-01-14T15:02:12Z to alias/old-audit-key followed by a GenerateDataKey to alias/new-audit-key. Looks like double-wrap during rotation. Consumer only knows new-audit-key, so old-wrapped bytes fail.
andrew: That explains the partial missing events spread across files: some producers used old key wrap (lib v1), others lib v2 after a staggered rollout.
support-nyc: Customer asks for a timeline and whether we can restore the missing events. ETA?
kevin: Short-term remediation: 1) Reprocess failed objects by decrypting server-side using the legacy key (we have backup CMK) and re-upload with correct envelope. 2) Add a compatibility shim in consumer to accept double-wrapped envelopes for a month. 3) Notify customers of incident and provide a re-ingest job.
oncall-sec: Action items: kevin -> run reprocess for s3://.../part-0007.avro + any files with put-object success but consumer decrypt errors. maria -> open rollback on the key-policy change and coordinate with crypto team to ensure backward compatibility. andrew -> draft initial customer-facing note: root cause key rotation race caused some batches to be double-wrapped; we will reprocess and deliver missing events within 48h.
andrew: Customer asked about retention: they want 7 years vs our default 90 days. We can't retroactively re-ingest beyond their retention window if we don't have objects. Confirmed we still have the original files in glacier-standard? kevin?
kevin: Files are in standard S3 for 30 days then standard-IA transition policy at 31 days -> not in Glacier yet for Jan 14. We can reprocess.
maria: For SIEM schema mapping: I'll export a sample successful event and the problematic one so mapping team can create a tolerant mapping (handle nulls for request.user_agent).
support-nyc: Thanks team — please keep case# 98721 updated. Customer wants a data proof-of-delivery once reprocessed.
andrew: I'll update the ticket after we re-upload. Closing loop: root cause = key rotation race causing mixed envelope formats -> consumer decrypt failures -> perceived missing events + schema flattening edgecases. Temporary mitigations in progress.
oncall-sec: Logging note: add an alert for forwarder-upload-success but consumer-decrypt-failure > 1 in 10 minutes for any tenant. Also add CloudTrail check to rotation runbooks.
kevin: Will do. I'll start the reprocess run and post progress.
sarah: reopening if we see other tenants affected.
